query: For additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs degradation during elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases and why catastrophic failure may occur? Specify a controlled change that would reveal the governing behavior, predicted observations relative to the starting-state baseline, applicable exposure boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: During exposure of additively-manufactured (AM) Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 to 800–950 °C oxidising or moderately reducing gases, degradation is governed by rapid Al- and Ti-selective internal oxidation that travels along AM-generated cellular solidification sub-structures (dislocation‐rich cell walls and interdendritic segregation bands).  These paths accumulate brittle (Al,Ti)-rich oxide/nitride stringers and voids.  Once a critical through-thickness volume fraction (~15–20 %) of these embrittling oxides is reached, load transfer to the remaining fcc matrix causes crack coalescence and sudden, catastrophic failure.
generation.material_initial_state: Laser powder-bed-fused Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3, as-built, fcc matrix with nanoscale cellular substructure, interdendritic enrichment of Al+Ti, and ~0.5 % residual porosity.
generation.intervention: Eliminate the AM cellular sub-structure without changing average composition by hot-isostatic pressing followed by a 1200 °C/2 h homogenisation and water-quench (HIP-homogenise).
generation.conditions: Isothermal exposure for 100 h in (a) lab air (pO2≈0.21 atm) and (b) 5 %H2–Ar (pO2≈10-18 atm) at 900 °C; identical mechanical bend tests afterwards at 25 °C.
generation.structural_mediator: Continuity and density of cellular dislocation/segregation walls that serve as fast diffusion pathways for O/N and sites for (Al,Ti) oxide/nitride precipitation.
generation.mechanism: 1. Al and Ti segregated to cell walls.  2. High defect density at walls provides fast inward O (or N) transport.  3. Internal oxidation/nitridation forms brittle (Al,Ti)(O,N) platelets + Kirkendall porosity along walls.  4. Local load shedding promotes micro-crack linkage; once oxide/void network spans ~15 – 20 % of section, catastrophic fracture occurs.  HIP-homogenisation removes these walls, suppressing fast-path diffusion and delaying oxide stringer formation, so failure is postponed.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the as-built baseline, HIP-homogenised samples will show: (i) ≥5× lower mass-gain rate, (ii) ≥3× shallower internal-oxide penetration depth, (iii) ≥50 % higher retained room-temperature bend strength after 100 h exposure, and (iv) absence of sudden load-drop (catastrophic fracture) within the first 1 mm of cross-head displacement.
generation.baseline: As-built coupons exposed and tested under identical conditions show parabolic mass gain ~4 mg cm⁻² after 100 h, internal oxidation to ~60 µm depth, and fail catastrophically at <0.3 % strain.
generation.boundary: Temperature 750–1000 °C; pO2 10-18 to 0.21 atm; exposure ≤200 h.  Outside this window (e.g., ≥1100 °C or pO2<10-20 atm) mechanisms may shift to external scale formation or evaporation-condensation.
generation.uncertainty: No direct data yet link AM cellular networks to internal oxidation in this specific HEA; magnitude of oxide-penetration reduction may differ.  Effect of residual porosity versus segregation pathways is not yet isolated.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare paired sets of coupons (as-built vs HIP-homogenised).  Expose both to 900 °C in air and 5 %H2–Ar for 10, 50, 100 h.  Measure (1) mass change vs time, (2) cross-sectional oxide penetration by SEM/EDS on polished mounts, (3) distribution of oxides relative to former cell walls (TEM/EBSD), (4) room-temperature 3-point bend strength and strain to failure.
measurements: Fractography identification of crack initiation sites
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If HIP-homogenised specimens show (a) ≤20 % reduction in oxide penetration depth OR (b) catastrophic fracture behaviour (sudden load drop) within ±10 % of the strain of as-built material, THEN the hypothesis is falsified.
